message.content:
Fix two real bugs found in a live Nxeon lift-and-shift migration (/opt/nxeon, `worker/migrate-real.ts`). A real migration to an Ubuntu 22.04 target failed on Docker install and DB import. Preserve all existing injection-safety (allowlist validators, secrets via file/STDIN, timeouts, per-migration work dir) — these are targeted fixes, not a rewrite.

## Bug 1 — Docker didn't install (wrong package path on Ubuntu)
Log showed: `Docker Engine + compose: could not install — bash: dnf: command not found  yum: command not found`. Root cause: `ensurePackages`/the prereq install maps the `docker` key to apt packages like `docker.io docker-compose-plugin`, but **`docker-compose-plugin` is NOT in Ubuntu's default apt repo**, so `apt-get install` returned non-zero and the code fell through to the `dnf`/`yum` branches (which don't exist on Debian/Ubuntu) → Docker never installed → all `docker compose up` steps failed with "docker: not found" and 0 containers came up.

Fix: install Docker via the official convenience script — the SAME method the platform's own provisioning uses (see `buildCloudInit` in `worker/index.ts`: `curl -fsSL https://get.docker.com | sh`), which adds Docker's repo and installs `docker-ce` + the compose plugin across Debian/Ubuntu/RHEL. So for the `docker` prerequisite specifically, run `curl -fsSL https://get.docker.com | sh` (then `systemctl enable --now docker`) instead of the apt/dnf package list. Keep it best-effort + logged; if the script fails, log honestly and continue. (Leave the other packages — nginx/apache/db engines/runtimes — on their existing apt/dnf/yum path; only Docker needs the script.) The command is a fixed constant — no source-provided input in it.

## Bug 2 — DB import failed on the MySQL system schema
Log showed: dump succeeded but import failed with `ERROR 1728 (HY000) ... Cannot load from mysql.proc. The table is probably corrupted`. Root cause: the source dump used `mysqldump --all-databases`, which INCLUDES MySQL's internal system schemas (`mysql`, `information_schema`, `performance_schema`, `sys`); restoring the source's `mysql` schema into a different-version engine corrupts/aborts the import.

Fix: dump only the USER databases. On the source, enumerate databases excluding the system schemas, e.g. `mysql -N -e "SHOW DATABASES"` filtered to drop `mysql`, `information_schema`, `performance_schema`, `sys` (all via root local/socket auth, no password — same as now), then `mysqldump --single-transaction --routines --triggers --events --databases <user db list>` into the work-dir dump. Validate each DB name against the existing identifier allowlist before it goes into the command (reject-not-sanitize; never interpolate an unvalidated SHOW DATABASES value). On the target, import that dump as root; add `--force` on the import as a safety so one bad statement doesn't abort the whole restore, and log clearly. If there are zero user databases, skip cleanly. (Postgres path via `pg_dumpall` can stay, but if trivial, similarly prefer per-database `pg_dump` excluding template0/template1 — only if low-risk; otherwise leave Postgres as-is and note it.)

## Constraints
- Preserve the injection-safe patterns exactly; the DB-name list must be allowlist-validated before use. The get.docker.com command is a fixed string. No schema change. No new deps. Do NOT touch mail/billing/terminal/cpanel/backup/marketing files or the wizard UI — just the migration engine (`worker/migrate-real.ts`, and `worker/migrate-detect.ts` only if you need a tiny read-only helper). Do NOT run git or `npm run build`.
- Write/Edit may time out on a hook — fall back to Bash heredocs and verify.
- Verify ONLY with `cd /opt/nxeon && npx tsc --noEmit 2>&1 | grep -v "test/.*test.ts"` (clean for your files).

Report: the exact Docker-install change (get.docker.com), the user-DB-only dump/import change (+ allowlist validation + --force), and confirm no other behavior changed.

content.text: Typecheck is clean. Both fixes are in place. Let me do a final review of the changed regions.

Both bugs are fixed in `/opt/nxeon/worker/migrate-real.ts`, typecheck clean, no schema/dep changes, no other files touched.

## Bug 1 — Docker install (get.docker.com)
In `ensurePackages`, the `docker` key is now special-cased inside the install loop. Instead of the apt/dnf/yum package list (which failed on Ubuntu because `docker-compose-plugin` isn't in Ubuntu's default apt repo, causing `apt-get install` to return non-zero and fall through to the nonexistent `dnf`/`yum` branches), `docker` now runs the fixed constant:
```
curl -fsSL https://get.docker.com | sh && systemctl enable --now docker
```
This is the same method `buildCloudInit` in `worker/index.ts` uses (adds Docker's repo, installs `docker-ce` + compose plugin across Debian/Ubuntu/RHEL). It stays best-effort + logged: it still runs through the same `PKG_CHECK` re-probe and pushes `installed`/`failed` into the summary. All other package keys (nginx/apache/db/runtimes) keep their existing apt→dnf→yum path unchanged. The command contains no source-supplied input.

## Bug 2 — DB import (user DBs only + allowlist + --force)
The MySQL branch no longer uses `mysqldump --all-databases` (which dumped the source's `mysql`/`information_schema`/`performance_schema`/`sys` schemas and corrupted the restore with ERROR 1728). It now:
1. Enumerates source databases via root LOCAL socket auth (no password), same as before: `${priv}mysql -N -e "SHOW DATABASES"` run through the existing `onSource()` wrapper.
2. Drops the four system schemas (case-insensitive) and validates every remaining name against a new `IDENT_RE = /^[A-Za-z0-9_]{1,64}$/` allowlist — reject, never sanitize — before it can enter any command. `IDENT_RE` deliberately mirrors `DBNAME_RE` in `migrate-detect.ts` (whose comment already referenced this constant).
3. Dumps only validated user DBs: `mysqldump --single-transaction --routines --triggers --events --databases <names>`.
4. Imports with `mysql --force < dump` so one bad statement can't abort the whole restore.
5. Handles edge cases cleanly: zero user DBs → `skipped` status ("only system schemas present"); listing failure → `failed`. Both use `continue` in the engine loop.

## Preserved / unchanged
- All injection-safety intact: DB names allowlist-validated before use, secrets still via SFTP 0600 file + `sshpass -f`, DB dumps via root local/socket auth (no password), per-migration work dir, timeouts, `finally` password scrub.
- The get.docker.com command is a fixed string; no source input flows into it.
- PostgreSQL path left as-is (per instructions — `pg_dumpall` change was not low-risk enough to justify). No schema changes, no new deps. No git/build run. Only `worker/migrate-real.ts` was modified (`migrate-detect.ts` needed no edit — its `IDENT_RE` cross-reference is now satisfied).
